date_note: Open's article of 27 November gives no earlier day for the attack.

evidence.quote: Hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and cold rooms holding cured meats worth about €250,000.

exec: Reported tampering with cold-storage controls at a food producer, with products worth about €250,000 affected.
geo_basis: victim city as stated by the source
plain: Hackers reportedly changed the settings of fridges and cold rooms at a cured-meat producer in Tolmin, Slovenia. Police are investigating, and nobody has claimed it.
summary: Open reports, citing company director Nikola Šavle speaking to 24ur.com, that hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and cold rooms holding cured meats worth about €250,000 at Alpija in Tolmin, Slovenia. A technician trying to reach the cooling system saw a lock screen with a photo of Matteo Salvini. Open says no one has claimed it and police in Nova Gorica are investigating.
title: Hackers reportedly raise temperatures in cold rooms of Slovenian cured-meat producer Alpija

validation.note: Single publisher: Open (Italy), relaying 24ur.com; Corriere's page could not be loaded and cedarnews and zazoom relay Open. The 24ur original was not read.
